cultural.summary: Boost seed immunity right from the start using local Himachal methods!
cultural.how: Soak seeds in cow urine before sowing, especially for kharif-season crops.

cultural.summary: Hang yellow sticky cards near the plant canopy to catch sap-sucking whiteflies.
cultural.how: Hang near plant canopy to monitor and trap whitefly vectors.

cultural.summary: Remove sick plants right away so the Vata imbalance doesn't spread!
cultural.how: Remove and destroy entire plant immediately on symptom appearance.

biological.summary: A powerful classical fermented tonic of dairy and cow urine to restore root strength.
biological.how: Ferment cow milk, curd, ghee, cow urine, and cow dung. Dilute and irrigate the root zone.

biological.summary: Purify the air around the leaves using traditional Ayurvedic fumigation.
biological.how: Burn dried neem leaves near the plant and allow the smoke to pass near the foliage.

biological.summary: Soapy neem bath prevents whiteflies from spreading the curl virus.
biological.how: Mix 5 ml neem oil with a couple of drops of liquid soap in 1 litre water. Spray whole plant.

cultural.summary: A simple, local Himachal trick to dry out fungi around the roots!
cultural.how: Dust wood ash directly around the base of the plant.

cultural.summary: Use fallen pine needles as a protective mulch layer over the soil.
cultural.how: Spread Pinus roxburgii needles around the base of the plant, 5-7cm thick.

biological.summary: A soothing classical Pitta-balancing decoction to cool the plant's system.
biological.how: Prepare a decoction of Yashtimadhu (licorice root) and Madhuca, mix with milk and honey, and irrigate.

biological.summary: A local farm-made pesticide paste applied right to the soil.
biological.how: Mix cow dung with water and apply to the plant/soil as a natural pesticide.

cultural.summary: Give plants plenty of personal space to dry out excess Kapha moisture.
cultural.how: Ensure adequate spacing at planting for maximum airflow.

cultural.summary: A clever local trick from Bilaspur to trap pests using fermented dairy!
cultural.how: Set out containers of buttermilk around the crop to act as local pest traps.

biological.summary: Diluted milk under morning sun creates a natural antiseptic action against white mildew.
biological.how: Mix 1 part milk with 9 parts water. Spray on leaves in morning sunlight.

cultural.summary: Enrich the soil with bitter neem cake to make it hostile for root worms.
cultural.how: Mix neem cake into the soil before planting.
cultural.frequency: Once at planting, refresh every 2-3 months

cultural.summary: Beautiful marigold roots naturally repel hidden nematodes!
cultural.how: Plant marigolds near or before transplanting tomatoes.

biological.summary: A classical shock-and-heal treatment for infested root zones.
biological.how: Irrigate with cold water for 7 consecutive days, then apply a cow dung, water, and milk paste to roots.

biological.summary: A potent Ayurvedic herbal paste applied directly to affected plant parts.
biological.how: Combine white mustard, Vacha, and Kushta into a paste. Apply directly to affected root/plant part.

cultural.summary: Protect stems from tools and heavy wind to prevent pathogen entry points.
cultural.how: Handle plants gently during pruning and weeding.

biological.summary: A classical Ayurvedic band-aid for cracked or wounded stems!
biological.how: Combine banyan bark, cluster fig bark, cow dung, honey, and ghee into a paste. Apply directly to the wound.
biological.frequency: Once, or as needed until healed
